Presenting complaints in this 73-year-old female include epigastric pain and nausea. Relatives noted vomiting earlier today.
COVID-19: ruled out clinically. Had Alzheimer's disease several years ago, now cured. Inj. ondansetron 8 mg IV given stat. At presentation, temp 100 F, BP 167/105 mmHg, HR 122 bpm, and the patient had constipation. Probable acute pancreatitis given the presentation. Established diagnosis of acute cholecystitis was made. Tracheostomy was not performed. Dose of mesalazine adjusted to 800 mg three times daily.

A 84-year-old female walked in with tremors; there was also weight gain. Takes tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled OD regularly. Probable PE given the presentation. Established diagnosis of obesity was made. Radioactive iodine ablation was not performed. Symptomatic improvement noted; cold intolerance resolved.

Presenting complaints in this 69-year-old male include neck stiffness and fainting episode. Relatives noted paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea earlier today. Aortic stenosis: ruled out clinically. Childhood history of heart attack.
No family history of HTN.
Propranolol 20 mg BID was tried earlier without benefit.
Takes metoprolol 50 mg PO twice daily regularly. The patient was alert and oriented. temp 102 F, BP 167/82 mmHg, HR 119 bpm. Troponin I: not performed. r/o pericarditis, awaiting results.
Coronary artery disease: established on the basis of the work-up.
Recovery after angioplasty was smooth.

Presenting complaints in this 20-year-old female include deformity of the limb and wrist pain. Relatives noted paraesthesia earlier today. Not associated with joint tenderness or hip pain. Inj. diclofenac 75 mg intramuscularly given stat. Repeat CRP after 48 hours showed a raised level of 72 mg/L. r/o lumbar spondylosis, awaiting results. Recovery after lumbar puncture was smooth.

Presenting complaints in this 58-year-old female include melaena and vomiting. Not associated with wheeze or chest tightness. Father had cerebral infarction; mother had acute appendicitis. Takes metronidazole 400 mg orally three times daily regularly.
A 68-year-old male walked in with left arm pain; there was also dizziness. Non-contrast CT brain: not performed. r/o RHD, awaiting results.

A 25-year-old male walked in with wheeze; there was also breathlessness on exertion. Relatives noted pleuritic chest pain earlier today. ILD: ruled out clinically. Doxycycline 100 mg BID was tried earlier without benefit. Pleural aspiration was not performed.

Presenting complaints in this 26-year-old female include nausea and dysphagia.
Relatives noted loss of appetite earlier today. Not associated with loose stools or vomiting.
Childhood history of ulcerative colitis. Pantoprazole 40 mg OD was tried earlier without benefit. Inj. metronidazole 500 mg intravenously given stat.
The patient was alert and oriented. respiratory rate 25/min, SpO2 93%, pulse 78/min. CT scan of the wrist: not performed. Probable acute gastroenteritis given the presentation. Hyponatremia: established on the basis of the work-up.
Liver biopsy was not performed.
Symptomatic improvement noted; haematemesis resolved.

A 54-year-old female walked in with loss of consciousness; there was also PND. Shortness of breath and fainting episode were present on arrival. Hypertension: ruled out clinically. Takes enoxaparin 40 mg SC once daily regularly. H. pylori stool antigen test: not performed. Probable bronchiectasis given the presentation. Coronary angiogram was not performed.

A 79-year-old male walked in with excessive thirst; there was also tiredness. Relatives noted cold intolerance earlier today. Not associated with weight gain or wrist pain. Had vitamin D deficiency several years ago, now cured. No family history of ulcerative colitis. No prior exposure to vitamin D3. TFTs: not performed. Probable T1DM given the presentation. Osteoporosis: established on the basis of the work-up. Recovery after radioiodine therapy was smooth. Symptomatic improvement noted; muscle weakness resolved.

Presenting complaints in this 36-year-old male include hip pain and wrist pain. Joint tenderness and morning stiffness were present on arrival. Childhood history of anterior cruciate ligament tear. Inj. cefazolin 1 g intravenously given stat. Repeat serum uric acid after 48 hours showed a level of 5.1 mg/dL. Probable Guillain-Barre syndrome given the presentation. Carpal tunnel syndrome: established on the basis of the work-up. Intra-articular steroid injection was not performed. Dose of tramadol adjusted to 50 mg QID.

A 50-year-old male walked in with hoarseness of voice; there was also fever. Omeprazole 20 mg OD was tried earlier without benefit. Takes tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled once daily regularly.
The patient was alert and oriented. temp 98 F, BP 101/79 mmHg, HR 70 bpm.
COVID RT-PCR: not performed. r/o SARS-CoV-2 infection, awaiting results. HTN: established on the basis of the work-up. Recovery after non-invasive ventilation was smooth.
Symptomatic improvement noted; chest tightness resolved.
Presenting complaints in this 65-year-old male include severe abdominal pain and vomiting. Not associated with high-grade fever or haematemesis. Dose of ondansetron adjusted to 4 mg stat.

Relatives noted chest tightness earlier today. Bronchogenic carcinoma: ruled out clinically.
Childhood history of COVID-19. Father had asthma; mother had ILD. No prior exposure to azithromycin. Repeat HRCT chest after 48 hours showed ground-glass opacities in both lower lobes.
Probable femur fracture given the presentation. Established diagnosis of pleural effusion was made. Dose of ceftriaxone adjusted to 1 g once daily.

Presenting complaints in this 36-year-old male include vomiting and loose stools. r/o Crohn's disease, awaiting results. Established diagnosis of ulcerative colitis was made. Laparoscopic appendicectomy was not performed.

Repeat chest X-ray after 48 hours showed an enlarged cardiac silhouette. Probable hypertension given the presentation. Congestive heart failure: established on the basis of the work-up.

Not associated with hemiparesis or memory loss. Childhood history of Guillain-Barre syndrome.

Repeat MRI of the brain after 48 hours showed no focal lesion. Probable migraine given the presentation. ICH: established on the basis of the work-up.
Burr hole drainage was not performed.

Repeat oral glucose tolerance test after 48 hours showed a 2-hour value of 126 mg/dL. Cushing's syndrome: established on the basis of the work-up. Recovery after total thyroidectomy was smooth. Symptomatic improvement noted; fatigue resolved.

Presenting complaints in this 84-year-old male include unintentional weight loss and difficulty breathing.

Father had anaphylaxis; mother had pulmonary embolism. Inj. morphine 5 mg IV given stat. The patient was alert and oriented. temp 97 F, BP 180/81 mmHg, HR 121 bpm. ABG: not performed. Probable hypovolemic shock given the presentation.

NG tube insertion was not performed.
Symptomatic improvement noted; profuse sweating resolved.

Inj. enoxaparin 40 mg SC given stat. At presentation, respiratory rate 23/min, SpO2 91%, pulse 96/min, and the patient had fatigue. Repeat creatinine after 48 hours showed a value of 2.1 mg/dL. r/o adrenal insufficiency, awaiting results.
Established diagnosis of dengue fever was made. PRBC transfusion was not performed. Symptomatic improvement noted; headache resolved.

Presenting complaints in this 79-year-old female include knee pain and deformity of the limb. Not associated with numbness in the fingers or lower back pain. No prior exposure to etoricoxib. At presentation, temp 103 F, BP 159/101 mmHg, HR 118 bpm, and the patient had joint swelling. Repeat CT wrist after 48 hours showed a comminuted pattern of the distal radius. Recovery after TKR was smooth. Symptomatic improvement noted; hip pain resolved.

No prior exposure to ceftriaxone. Takes ASA 75 mg PO once daily regularly. Repeat CT head after 48 hours showed a hyperdense lesion in the right basal ganglia. Intravenous thrombolysis was not performed.

Father had type 2 diabetes mellitus; mother had appendicitis. Inj. pantoprazole 40 mg IV given stat. Total bilirubin: not performed. Recovery after colonoscopy was smooth. Relatives noted loss of appetite earlier today. Not associated with generalised weakness or heartburn. Had Type 2 Diabetes several years ago, now cured. Repeat ECG after 48 hours showed an irregularly irregular rhythm at 118 bpm. Probable AFib given the presentation. Osteomyelitis: established on the basis of the work-up.

Inj. pantoprazole 80 mg IV given stat. At presentation, temp 101 F, BP 176/69 mmHg, HR 63 bpm, and the patient had exertional fatigue. Established diagnosis of anaphylaxis was made.
